label: shared_mechanism
rationale: 'Disturbed sleep ... associated with an increased probability of syndrome onset' describes a shared risk-factor/mechanism for developing these functional syndromes, not that patients already have both diagnoses.
finding_text: Disturbed sleep at baseline was a shared predictor of new onset for all three syndromes, though the effect sizes were small.
provenance_quote: Disturbed sleep (PSQI score), greater stress related to chronic ill health, higher somatization score (SCL-90 SOM) and poor perception of general health (RAND scale) were associated with an increased probability of syndrome onset.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Somatization score is listed among shared predictors of 'syndrome onset' for IBS/CFS/FM, a mechanism-level link rather than a comorbidity claim.
finding_text: Higher somatization score (SCL-90 SOM) at baseline was a shared predictor of onset of IBS, CFS and FM.
provenance_quote: Disturbed sleep (PSQI score), greater stress related to chronic ill health, higher somatization score (SCL-90 SOM) and poor perception of general health (RAND scale) were associated with an increased probability of syndrome onset.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Poor general-health perception is part of the same shared-predictor cluster for 'syndrome onset', a mechanism-level association.
finding_text: Poorer perception of general health (RAND General Health scale) at baseline predicted new onset of all three syndromes.
provenance_quote: Disturbed sleep (PSQI score), greater stress related to chronic ill health, higher somatization score (SCL-90 SOM) and poor perception of general health (RAND scale) were associated with an increased probability of syndrome onset.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Text explicitly states 'these two syndromes shared a cluster of predictors related to allergy', a shared-mechanism claim without asserting patient co-occurrence.
finding_text: Use of nasal decongestants at baseline predicted new-onset fibromyalgia, part of a shared allergy-related cluster with IBS.
provenance_quote: these two syndromes shared a cluster of predictors related to allergy (including having an allergy for both IBS and FM, medication for obstructive airway diseases for IBS, and nasal decongestants for FM).

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: IL-6 positively predicts a combined fibromyalgia/fatigue (FF) severity score, linking the two conditions via a common inflammatory marker rather than asserting comorbidity.
finding_text: Plasma IL-6 was positively and independently associated with the fibromyalgia/chronic fatigue (FF) symptom score in schizophrenia patients.
provenance_quote: A large part of the variance in the FF score (55.1%) is explained by the regression on digit sequencing task, token motor task, list learning, IL-10, age (all inversely) and IL-6 (positively).

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: IL-10 is inversely associated with the same combined FF score, a shared-biomarker mechanism link between fibromyalgia and CFS-type fatigue.
finding_text: Plasma IL-10 was inversely and independently associated with the FF symptom score, suggesting lowered immune regulation contributes to physiosomatic symptoms.
provenance_quote: A large part of the variance in the FF score (55.1%) is explained by the regression on digit sequencing task, token motor task, list learning, IL-10, age (all inversely) and IL-6 (positively).

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Quote 'Physiosomatic symptoms are an integral part of the phenome of schizophrenia' links FM/CFS-like symptom clusters to schizophrenia phenotype via mechanism/phenomenology, not an explicit patient comorbidity claim.
finding_text: The paper's overarching conclusion is that chronic-fatigue/fibromyalgia-like physiosomatic symptoms, as measured by the FF scale, are an integral component of the schizophrenia phenome rather than an incidental comorbidity.
provenance_quote: Physiosomatic symptoms are an integral part of the phenome of schizophrenia.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Quote states FM and CFS 'may share the same pathophysiological mechanism' (elevated CSF pressure via Tarlov cysts) — a mechanism link, not a patient co-occurrence claim.
finding_text: The authors conclude that TC prevalence in FM/CFS patients was three times higher than in the general population, supporting a shared pathophysiology between symptomatic Tarlov cysts and FM/CFS involving elevated cerebrospinal fluid pressure irritating dorsal root ganglia.
provenance_quote: In patients diagnosed with FM or CFS, the prevalence of TCs was three times higher than that in the general population. This observation supports the hypothesis that STCs, FM, and CFS may share the same pathophysiological mechanism, i.e., moderately increased cerebrospinal fluid pressure, causing irritation of neurons and axons in dorsal root ganglia.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Gene expression changes (ASIC3, P2RX4/5) are reported specifically in an ME/CFS-with-comorbid-fibromyalgia subgroup, tying a molecular mechanism to the co-occurring conditions rather than newly asserting the comorbidity itself.
finding_text: After moderate exercise, ME/CFS patients with comorbid fibromyalgia showed greater increases than healthy controls in gene expression of metabolite-sensing DRG receptors ASIC3 and P2X purinoreceptors 4 and 5.
provenance_quote: Patients showed greater increases than controls in gene expression for metabolite detecting DRG receptors including acid-sensing ion channel 3, and P2X purinoreceptor 4 and 5.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: DEGs are 'enriched for genes associated with stress-induced MC activation in IBS', a molecular mechanism link between mast cell activation and IBS.
finding_text: Bioinformatics analysis of the CGRP-induced DEGs in mast cells showed enrichment for genes involved in response to corticotropin-releasing hormone, regulation of transcription, mast cell activation, and mast cell proliferation, overlapping with genes implicated in stress-induced mast cell activation in IBS.
provenance_quote: Bioinformatics analysis showed that key higher DEGs included those associated with response to corticotropin-releasing hormone (CRH), regulation of transcription, MC activation, and proliferation. These processes are enriched for genes associated with stress-induced MC activation in IBS.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: 'brainstem dysfunction has been implicated in other similar disorders, such as chronic pain and migraine and ... chronic fatigue syndrome' links via shared mechanism, not patient co-occurrence.
finding_text: Brainstem dysfunction has previously been implicated in other chronic disorders with symptom overlap, including chronic pain, migraine, and myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS).
provenance_quote: Indeed, brainstem dysfunction has been implicated in other similar disorders, such as chronic pain and migraine and myalgic encephalomyelitis or chronic fatigue syndrome.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: '3-fold increased prevalence of psychological trauma' in these syndromes describes a shared antecedent/risk factor, not co-occurrence of the two conditions with each other.
finding_text: A prior meta-analysis found a 3-fold increased prevalence of psychological trauma in patients with functional somatic syndromes, including IBS, fibromyalgia, and chronic fatigue syndrome, compared to healthy controls.
provenance_quote: For example, a meta-analysis by Afari et al. (24) showed a 3-fold increased prevalence of psychological trauma in patients with functional somatic syndromes such as irritable bowel syndrome, fibromyalgia, or chronic fatigue syndrome compared to healthy controls.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: 'Less than 20% of participants had autoantibodies known to be associated with dysautonomia' reports a biomarker link to dysautonomia in an EDS/HSD cohort, not a diagnosed-comorbidity claim.
finding_text: Fewer than 20% of hEDS GENE study participants had autoantibodies known to be associated with dysautonomia, suggesting these autoantibodies are not a major driver of symptoms in most participants.
provenance_quote: Less than 20% of participants had autoantibodies known to be associated with dysautonomia.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Quote describes a proposed shared genetic mechanism (TPSAB1 duplication raising tryptase from mast cell activity) rather than asserting patients have both diagnosed conditions; POTS/EDS not even named in the quote itself.
finding_text: The paper cites literature suggesting that germline duplications/triplications of TPSAB1 encoding alpha-tryptase raise basal serum tryptase and may underlie opioid intolerance and the co-occurrence of MCAS, POTS, and EDS-HT/JHS.
provenance_quote: it is striking that some studies seem to suggest there is a common genetic condition related to germline excessive duplications and triplications in the allelic TPSAB1 gene encoding α-tryptase that provokes an increase in serum basal tryptase levels from mast cell activity (tryptase ≥ 8.0 ng/ml).

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Quote describes symptom-criteria overlap ('ME/CFS case definitions... reported by...long COVID studies') rather than patients carrying both formal diagnoses.
finding_text: Fatigue was the most frequently reported long COVID symptom across the selected studies, noted in 13 of 21 eligible studies (also cited as 12 of 21 in the discussion).
provenance_quote: All three major criteria symptoms as specified by most ME/CFS case definitions (fatigue, reduced daily activity, post-exertional malaise) were reported by multiple selected long COVID studies, with fatigue being the most reported symptom (13 out of 21 eligible studies).

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Proposes activated mast cells 'up-regulate the function of PAR-2... leading to clinical symptoms' in IBS-D — a mechanistic link, not a claim that patients carry both diagnoses.
finding_text: The authors propose a mechanistic model in which activated mast cells up-regulate PAR-2 function, altering neuropeptide (NPS/NPY) levels, which together drive clinical symptoms and psychological changes (anxiety/depression) in IBS-D.
provenance_quote: There might be a close connection among the activated MC, increased PAR-2, and reduced NPY and NPS in the IBS-D accompanied by anxiety or depression: the activated MC may up-regulate the function of PAR-2, resulting in the change of neuropeptide (NPS and NPY), successively leading to clinical symptoms and psychological negative changes in the IBS-D.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: 'Antibodies against muscarinic and adrenergic receptors...identified in ME/CFS and are thought to be associated with postural orthostatic symptoms' links the conditions via an autoantibody mechanism, not a comorbidity assertion.
finding_text: Antibodies against muscarinic and adrenergic receptors have been identified in ME/CFS and are thought to be associated with postural orthostatic symptoms.
provenance_quote: Antibodies against muscarinic and adrenergic receptors have been identified in ME/CFS and are thought to be associated with postural orthostatic symptoms.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: A COL1A2 variant 'previously reported as pathogenic for...osteogenesis imperfecta' was found in a patient clinically diagnosed with EDS — a shared genetic mechanism, not an assertion of two co-diagnosed conditions.
finding_text: A heterozygous COL1A2 c.2701G>A (p.Gly901Ser) variant, previously reported as pathogenic for moderate-severe and lethal osteogenesis imperfecta, was identified in a proband clinically diagnosed with Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.
provenance_quote: The analysis failed to find an alteration in COL5A1 and COL5A2 genes, but two heterozygous variants in collagen type I genes were identified: a c.133C>G (p.Leu45Val) in exon 2 of COL1A1 gene and a c.2701G>A (p.Gly901Ser) in exon 42 of COL1A2 gene.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: 'Anxiety or depression are common in these two diseases' identifies a shared associated feature linking fibromyalgia and small fiber neuropathy, without asserting the two occur together in the same patient.
finding_text: Anxiety and depression are common comorbidities in both fibromyalgia and small fibre neuropathy.
provenance_quote: Anxiety or depression are common in these two diseases, but post-traumatic stress disorder and physical or sexual abuse in childhood or adulthood suggest fibromyalgia.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Autoantibodies against M1 acetylcholine receptors (an autonomic receptor) demonstrated in ME/CFS patients links to a mechanistic marker rather than an assertion that patients carry a dysautonomia diagnosis.
finding_text: Autoantibodies against M1 acetylcholine receptors are demonstrated in ME/CFS patients and their occurrence is associated with reduced binding of M1 AChR ligand in the brain on PET imaging.
provenance_quote: In this context, it is of great interest that autoantibodies against the M1 acetylcholine receptors (AChR) were demonstrated in these patients. Occurrence of these autoantibodies was associated with reduced binding of M1 AChR ligand in brain analyzed by PET imaging [6, 7].

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: 89.1% of long-COVID participants reported PEM, 'a core ME/CFS diagnostic criterion' — symptom-criterion overlap, not an assertion of dual diagnosis.
finding_text: 89.1% of participants reported post-exertional malaise (worsening of symptoms after physical or mental activity), a core ME/CFS diagnostic criterion.
provenance_quote: 89.1% of participants (95% confidence interval 88.0% to 90.0%) reported experiencing either physical or mental PEM.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Cardiac chamber findings in hEDS/HSD-related dysautonomia are 'consistent with the previous reports in positional orthostatic tachycardia syndrome' — a shared physiological phenotype, not a claim that patients have both diagnoses.
finding_text: Cardiac chamber size and geometry findings in hEDS/HSD-related dysautonomia parallel prior reports of similar cardiac findings in POTS.
provenance_quote: JH-related dysautonomia was associated with smaller cardiac chamber sizes, consistent with the previous reports in positional orthostatic tachycardia syndrome.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: EBV DNA concentration 'positively associated with pain, neurocognition, and autonomic symptoms' within an ME/CFS subgroup — a biomarker link to autonomic symptom severity, not a dual-diagnosis claim.
finding_text: In the same stable-repertoire (pattern 2) severely affected ME/CFS subgroup, EBV DNA concentration was positively correlated with pain, neurocognition, and autonomic symptom scores.
provenance_quote: whereas, EBV DNA concentration was positively associated with pain, neurocognition, and autonomic symptoms (r = 0.48, 0.40, and 0.39, respectively, P = 0.001, 0.008, and 0.010, respectively).

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Post-COVID symptoms (fatigue, PEM, cognitive dysfunction) described as 'all common core symptoms of ME/CFS' — symptom overlap, not an assertion patients carry both diagnoses.
finding_text: In an international web-based survey (n=3,762) of post-COVID-19 patients at 6 months, 80% were female, with fatigue (>75%), post-exertional malaise (>69%) and cognitive dysfunction (>52%) as the most frequent symptoms.
provenance_quote: An international, web-based survey involved 3,762 participants, aged between 30 and 59 years old (13). Of those with post-COVID-19 issues, 6 months since their infection, 80% were female. The most frequently reported symptoms were fatigue (>75%), post-exertional malaise (>69%) and cognitive dysfunction (“brain-fog”) (>52%), all common core symptoms of ME/CFS.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Post-COVID-19 patients' symptoms are framed as 'the most frequently reported ME/CFS symptoms' — overlap in symptom criteria, not explicit dual diagnosis.
finding_text: A German clinical study of 42 post-COVID-19 patients found chronic fatigue in all 42, PEM in 41, cognitive impairment in 40, headache in 38, and muscle pain in 35.
provenance_quote: The most frequently reported ME/CFS symptoms were chronic fatigue by all 42 patients, post exertional malaise (PEM) (n = 41), cognitive impairment (n = 40), headache (n = 38), and muscle pain (n = 35).

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Fibromyalgia cortical glial-cell activation described with 'some overlap in cingulate cortex activation similar to ME/CFS' — shared mechanism, not comorbidity claim.
finding_text: A PET/MRI study of fibromyalgia found glial-cell activity elevated in the cortex relative to healthy controls, with some overlap in cingulate cortex activation similar to ME/CFS.
provenance_quote: A recent PET/MRI study of the closely-related fibromyalgia provided evidence that individual brain-signatures are achievable (37), as glial-cell activity in a different region, the cortex was elevated relative to healthy controls.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Speculative proposal that SARS-CoV-2 targets the hypothalamic PVN, 'previously proposed... in ME/CFS' — hypothesized shared mechanism, not a comorbidity assertion.
finding_text: The author proposes that SARS-CoV-2 infection acts as a severe physiological stressor targeting the hypothalamic paraventricular nucleus (PVN), previously proposed as the target site in ME/CFS, switching it into an ongoing dysfunctional mode in genetically susceptible individuals.
provenance_quote: It is proposed, therefore, that SARS-CoV-2 infection, in common with the triggers of ME/CFS, manifests itself as a severe physiological stressor. An essential target could be the brain's stress-center, a cluster of neurons in the hypothalamic paraventricular nucleus (PVN), which has been proposed previously to be the target site in ME/CFS (16, 17).

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Proposes long COVID 'no constituye una nueva entidad sino que es... una encefalomielitis miálgica' (symptom/biological-plausibility overlap), asserting shared identity/mechanism rather than that patients carry both diagnoses.
finding_text: The review proposes that long COVID (post-acute/persistent COVID syndrome) may overlap substantially with myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome as defined by the International Consensus Criteria, based on symptom comparison across multiple guideline sources.
provenance_quote: la similitud entre los cuadros y la plausibilidad biológica pueden ser orientativas para indicar que el síndrome de COVID persistente no constituye una nueva entidad sino que es, en realidad, en algunos casos, una encefalomielitis miálgica.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Links a biomarker (alpha-tryptase/TPSAB1, a MCAS-associated marker) to an hEDS-like symptom cluster, explicitly noting 'not all patients... met diagnostic criteria for hEDS' — a mechanistic/biomarker link, not an assertion of two co-occurring diagnoses.
finding_text: High alpha-tryptase levels linked to TPSAB1 gene mutations were found in patients with hEDS-like symptoms (connective tissue abnormalities, autonomic dysfunction, GI, allergic and cutaneous symptoms), though not all such patients met hEDS diagnostic criteria and elevated basal tryptase is common in the general population.
provenance_quote: Other gene mutations concern tpsab1, a gene encoding for alpha-tryptase, whose high levels were found in patients with symptoms easily found in hEDS patients (such as connective tissue abnormalities, autonomic dysfunction, gastrointestinal disorders, allergic, and cutaneous symptoms), although not all patients with tpsab1 mutations met diagnostic criteria for hEDS and elevated alpha-tryptase basal serum levels are quite common in the general population

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Proposes elevated prolactin as a shared nociceptive mechanism across migraine and EDS pain, explicitly flagged as 'speculative for EDS specifically' rather than a comorbidity claim.
finding_text: Elevated serum prolactin is associated with various pain conditions (migraine, RA, osteoarthritis) and may modulate nociceptor activity, suggesting a possible role in EDS-related chronic pain, though this link is speculative for EDS specifically.
provenance_quote: Literature data show how elevated serum prolactin (PRL) levels were associated with a variety of pain conditions (migraine, burning, rheumatoid arthritis, and osteoarthritis) and can modulate the activity of nociceptors, playing an important role in pain responses and inflammation.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Shows diet-induced change in mast-cell mediator (histamine/tryptase) levels in IBS-D patients — a mechanistic biomarker link, not an assertion of comorbid MCAS diagnosis.
finding_text: Serum histamine and mast cell tryptase levels were significantly reduced in IBS-D patients after a 4-week low-FODMAP diet.
provenance_quote: This was accompanied with significant reduction in serum levels of histamine and mast cell tryptase post-LFM diet (P = 0.033 and P = 0.049, respectively) (Figure 5B).

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Reports serum histamine (a mast-cell mediator) reduction with diet in IBS-D patients, a mechanistic biomarker link rather than a comorbidity claim.
finding_text: Serum histamine levels significantly decreased in IBS-D patients after a 4-week low-FODMAP diet.
provenance_quote: This was accompanied with significant reduction in serum levels of histamine and mast cell tryptase post-LFM diet (P = 0.033 and P = 0.049, respectively) (Figure 5B).

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Reports serum tryptase (a mast-cell mediator) reduction with diet in IBS-D patients, a mechanistic biomarker link rather than a comorbidity claim.
finding_text: Serum mast cell tryptase levels significantly decreased in IBS-D patients after a 4-week low-FODMAP diet.
provenance_quote: This was accompanied with significant reduction in serum levels of histamine and mast cell tryptase post-LFM diet (P = 0.033 and P = 0.049, respectively) (Figure 5B).

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Maternal systemic mastocytosis (mast-cell hyperactivity) linked to offspring ASD risk — a cross-generational mechanistic association, not two conditions co-occurring in the same patient.
finding_text: Children born to mothers with systemic mastocytosis, characterized by a greater number of hyperactive mast cells, had a higher risk of developing ASD.
provenance_quote: We reported that children born to mothers with systemic mastocytosis [63], which is characterized by a greater number of hyperactive mast cells than in the general population [197], had a higher risk of developing ASD [1,2,7,198,199].

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Duplicate of the maternal-mastocytosis/offspring-ASD mechanistic link; not a same-patient comorbidity claim.
finding_text: Children born to mothers with systemic mastocytosis, characterized by hyperactive mast cells, had a higher risk of developing ASD.
provenance_quote: We reported that children born to mothers with systemic mastocytosis [63], which is characterized by a greater number of hyperactive mast cells than in the general population [197], had a higher risk of developing ASD [1,2,7,198,199].

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Describes 'a dysregulation of the brain-gut axis resulting in a state of generalized hyperalgesia' as a proposed shared mechanism, without asserting patients have both conditions.
finding_text: A proposed shared mechanism for FM-IBS comorbidity is dysregulation of the brain-gut axis producing generalized hyperalgesia (central sensitivity), increasing excitability of central nociceptive pathways and inhibiting descending pain modulation.
provenance_quote: There is a hypothesis suggesting a dysregulation of the brain−gut axis resulting in a state of generalized hyperalgesia (also known as central sensitivity disorders) leading to increased excitability of central nociceptive pathways and inhibition of descending pain modulation [15].

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Describes ME/CFS pathophysiology including 'alteration of autonomic nervous system function, in particular sensitization of the sympathetic nervous system' as an internal feature, not an assertion that patients carry a separate dysautonomia diagnosis.
finding_text: ME/CFS is described as a multi-system disorder involving HPA axis dysregulation, autonomic sympathetic sensitization, orthostatic intolerance with reduced cerebral blood flow, abnormal cortisol/circadian rhythms, increased pro-inflammatory cytokines, altered muscle anaerobic threshold, post-exertional malaise, central sensitization, and grey/white matter brain changes.
provenance_quote: The range of abnormal responses includes alteration of autonomic nervous system function, in particular sensitization of the sympathetic nervous system, with lasting adaptations in energy metabolism and the immune response, orthostatic intolerance with reduction in cerebral blood flow on tilt testing, variations in cortisol levels associated with increased fatigue, disorganized circadian rhythms, increased immune system activation, as shown for example by increased pro-inflammatory cytokines and prolonged inflammatory responses, alterations in muscle anaerobic threshold, abnormal recovery after activity with post-exertional malaise, central sensitization, and changes in grey and white matter in the brain [5].

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Reports 'much overlap of symptoms between Long COVID-19 and ME/CFS ... and some common features in terms of pathophysiology' — a symptom/mechanism overlap claim, not a patient-level comorbidity assertion.
finding_text: A systematic review of twenty-one studies (Wong and Weitzer) reported substantial symptom overlap between Long COVID and ME/CFS, including fatigue, reduced daily activity and post-exertional malaise, and some shared pathophysiological features.
provenance_quote: A systemic review by Wong and Weitzer in this issue considered twenty-one studies, and reported much overlap of symptoms between Long COVID-19 and ME/CFS, including fatigue, reduced daily activity, and post-exertional malaise, and some common features in terms of pathophysiology [18].

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Proposes a shared taxonomic category 'post-active phase of infection syndromes' based on 'overlapping biological and clinical features', a mechanistic/classificatory overlap claim rather than a comorbidity assertion.
finding_text: Based on overlapping biological and clinical features, the authors propose a new taxonomic category, 'post-active phase of infection syndromes' (PAPIS), encompassing both Long COVID and ME/CFS.
provenance_quote: Such evidence has prompted the proposal of a new taxonomic classification, comprising both Long COVID and ME/CFS within a category entitled post-active phase of infection syndromes, or PAPIS [21].

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: States gene interaction analyses 'reveal extensive gene clustering that might represent a biological mechanism for the observed clinical overlap' between ASD and hypermobility — a mechanism claim, not patient-level comorbidity.
finding_text: Across monogenic genetic syndromes strongly associated with both autism and hypermobility, and known genetic causes of EDS subtypes, gene interaction analyses reveal extensive gene clustering that may represent a biological mechanism underlying the clinical overlap.
provenance_quote: More broadly, across monogenic genetic syndromes strongly associated with both ASD and hypermobility, and known genetic causes of EDS subtypes, analyses of gene interactions reveal extensive gene clustering that might represent a biological mechanisms for the observed clinical overlap[34].

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: States '40.00% [of fibromyalgia-related genes were associated] with pain sensitivity and/or migraine' — a gene-level/mechanistic overlap claim, not a patient comorbidity assertion.
finding_text: 40.00% of the fibromyalgia-related genes were also associated with pain sensitivity and/or migraine.
provenance_quote: and 40.00% with pain sensitivity and/or migraine, besides other disorders associated (drug addiction, autoimmune disorders, circulatory problems, and metabolic alterations).

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Finding centers on a shared physiological marker ('hypocapnia and hyperventilation') found in both cohorts, not a claim that patients hold both diagnoses.
finding_text: Hypocapnia and hyperventilation are frequently found in both ME/CFS and POTS.
provenance_quote: A frequent finding in ME/CFS and postural tachycardia syndrome (POTS), which is frequently associated with ME/CFS, is hypocapnia and hyperventilation [14, 39].

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Reports symptom overlap ('25 out of 29 symptoms' overlapping) between the two syndromes, a clinical-feature overlap rather than a claim that patients carry both diagnoses.
finding_text: A cited comparative analysis (Wong and Weitzer) found that 25 of 29 symptoms overlapped between post-COVID-19 syndrome and ME/CFS, including the three cardinal ME/CFS symptoms of fatigue, reduced daily activity, and post-exertional malaise.
provenance_quote: This analysis revealed a significant overlap in 25 out of 29 symptoms with the three major ME/CFS symptoms (fatigue, reduced daily activity, and post-exertional malaise) widely reported in the post-COVID-19 syndrome literature.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: A COL1A1 mosaic variant underlying a combined OI/EDS overlap presentation points to a shared collagen-gene mechanism rather than two independently comorbid diagnoses.
finding_text: Somatic mosaicism for a COL1A1 heterozygous pathogenic variant, undetectable in peripheral blood, was identified in an adult with osteogenesis imperfecta/Ehlers-Danlos syndrome overlap.
provenance_quote: Finally, somatic mosaicism for a COL1A1 heterozygous pathogenic variant absent in the peripheral blood was identified in an adult with osteogenesis imperfecta/Ehlers-Danlos syndrome overlap [19].

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Groups fibromyalgia and migraine together as conditions 'associated with multiple gene mutations', a shared polygenic mechanism claim rather than a patient-comorbidity claim.
finding_text: Fibromyalgia, along with migraine and hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathies, is described as being associated with multiple gene mutations rather than a single causative gene.
provenance_quote: Clinical syndromes of derangement of pain sensation are generally caused by single gene mutations (e.g. erythromelalgia and paroxysmal extreme pain disorder caused by mutations of SCN9A), but can also be associated with multiple gene mutations, as happens in migraine, fibromyalgia or hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathies.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Describes a cellular mechanism ("reduced axonal diameter and...abnormalities in Schwann cells") underlying small fiber pathology in fibromyalgia, not a diagnostic co-occurrence claim.
finding_text: Small fiber neuropathy in fibromyalgia patients is accompanied by reduced axonal diameter and Schwann cell abnormalities on electron microscopy.
provenance_quote: small fiber pathology in fibromyalgia patients was found to be accompanied by reduced axonal diameter and some abnormalities in Schwann cells seen on electron microscopy [200].

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Same mechanistic description of "reduced axonal diameter and...abnormalities in Schwann cells" in fibromyalgia-associated small fiber pathology.
finding_text: Small fiber pathology in fibromyalgia patients was found to be accompanied by reduced axonal diameter and abnormalities in Schwann cells on electron microscopy.
provenance_quote: According to this model, the answer is: neither- small fiber pathology in fibromyalgia patients was found to be accompanied by reduced axonal diameter and some abnormalities in Schwann cells seen on electron microscopy [200].

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Links CFS to "higher serum levels of autoantibodies against the autonomic receptors", a biomarker/mechanism connection rather than a comorbidity diagnosis claim.
finding_text: Chronic fatigue syndrome has been shown to be associated with higher serum levels of autoantibodies against autonomic receptors, such as beta-adrenergic and muscarinic receptors.
provenance_quote: In addition, CFS has been shown to be associated with higher serum levels of autoantibodies against the autonomic receptors, such as beta-adrenergic and muscarinic receptors

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: States shared symptoms of EDS "are considered by some as an overlap with chronic fatigue syndrome" — a phenotypic/symptom overlap claim rather than an assertion that patients carry both diagnoses.
finding_text: Fatigue, daytime sleepiness, joint pain, dislocation, recurrent injuries, dizziness, chronic pain, anxiety, dysautonomia, and phobic states are common symptoms of EDS that are considered by some to overlap with chronic fatigue syndrome and are also frequent in sleep-disordered breathing.
provenance_quote: Fatigue, daytime sleepiness, joint pain, dislocation and recurrent injuries, dizziness, chronic pain, anxiety, dysautonomia and phobic states are common symptoms of EDS and are considered by some as an overlap with chronic fatigue syndrome, they are also frequent symptoms in patients with sleep-disordered breathing (SDB).

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Reports endothelial dysfunction (RHI) as a biomarker elevated in post-COVID ME/CFS patients vs controls, linking the two via a physiological marker rather than asserting diagnostic co-occurrence per se.
finding_text: Five of 14 post-COVID ME/CFS patients had peripheral endothelial dysfunction (RHI ≤1.67) versus none of the healthy controls.
provenance_quote: Patient cohorts showed a significantly higher frequency of ED than the HC group (Fisher's exact test; pME/CFS = 0.0169 and pPCS = 0.0434).

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Low FODMAP diet 'improve[s] IBS symptoms... accompanied by... reduced mast cell activation,' linking IBS and mast cell activation mechanistically via a shared dietary/barrier pathway, not asserting comorbid diagnoses.
finding_text: Low FODMAP diets normalize fecal LPS levels and improve IBS symptoms in IBS-D patients, accompanied by improved colon barrier function and reduced mast cell activation.
provenance_quote: Subsequent studies in IBS‐D patients showed that low FODMAP diets normalize fecal LPS levels and improve IBS symptoms, accompanied by improved colon barrier functions and reduced mast cell activation.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Duplicate of the FODMAP diet finding: 'improved IBS symptoms... reduced mast cell activation' links the two mechanistically, not as co-diagnosed conditions.
finding_text: In IBS-D patients, low FODMAP diets normalized fecal LPS levels and improved IBS symptoms, accompanied by improved colon barrier function and reduced mast cell activation.
provenance_quote: Subsequent studies in IBS‐D patients showed that low FODMAP diets normalize fecal LPS levels and improve IBS symptoms, accompanied by improved colon barrier functions and reduced mast cell activation.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: IBS is described as 'related to SFN' with 'central sensitization to pain and itch,' framing the association as a shared small-fiber neuropathy mechanism rather than a diagnostic co-occurrence claim.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Proposes BH4-dependent neurotransmitter deficiencies 'tied to numerous dysfunctions... associated with PASC, including... dysautonomia, essential tremor, POTS, Ehlers Danlos syndrome,' a speculative shared-mechanism hypothesis spanning several conditions, not a patient comorbidity assertion.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: HSV-1 gastric DNA detected in '100% (30/30)' of FGID+FM patients vs '26.7%' of controls, proposing a shared viral mechanism underlying the comorbid state rather than asserting the comorbidity itself.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: ICP8 (active HSV-1 replication marker) detected in '83.3% (25/30)' of FGID+FM patients vs '6.7%' controls, supporting a shared infectious mechanism in the comorbid group.
finding_text: ICP8 protein, a marker of active HSV-1 lytic replication, was detected in 83.3% of FGID+FM patients versus 6.7% of controls.
provenance_quote: ICP8 was detected in the biopsies of 83.3% (25/30) of Group 1 patients, 73.3% (11/15) of Group 2 patients, and 6.7% (1/15) of control patients (Fig. 1B).

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Only speculatively notes circadian rhythm maintenance 'could in principle... alter[] the risk of PASC and ME/CFS' — a hedged, non-established mechanistic link.

provenance_quote: Ability to maintain physiological circadian rhythms has been associated with better outcomes in ICU (Davidson et al., 2021), and could in principle, protect patients from circadian disruption and possibly altering the risk of PASC and ME/CFS.

label: shared_mechanism

label: shared_mechanism

provenance_quote: Impairment of the microbiome–gut–brain interaction has been associated with multiple CNS and ENS related disorders such as ASD, anxiety, depression, Parkinson’s disease, and IBS (Israelyan and Margolis, 2018).

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Proposes epipharyngitis-driven cytokines (TNF-α, IFN-γ, IL-1) causing 'low-grade inflammation in the brain associated with ME/CFS' symptoms occurring in long COVID — a shared inflammatory mechanism claim.

label: shared_mechanism

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: MCAS and long COVID 'share clinical features' including overlapping symptoms and treatment response, a mechanistic/clinical-resemblance claim, not a patient co-occurrence claim.

label: shared_mechanism

finding_text: A higher n-6/n-3 PUFA ratio was associated with a greater number of overlapping nociplastic pain conditions.
provenance_quote: In multiple linear regression, each unit increase in n-6/n-3 PUFA ratio was associated with more pain conditions (β = 0.30, 95% confidence limits: 0.07, 0.53, p = 0.012).

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Higher frequency of EDS-associated gene variants (COL5A1, TNXB) in idiopathic gastroparesis patients is a shared genetic/mechanistic link, not an assertion that patients carry both diagnoses.

provenance_quote: Interestingly, we report a significantly higher frequency of variants in COL5A1, TNXB, and nominally significant COL1A2 in the patients with idiopathic gastroparesis (Table 2).

label: shared_mechanism

provenance_quote: Remarkably, mannose binding lectin (MBL) deficiency, which is associated with enhanced susceptibility to infections and was found previously more frequently in ME/CFS (15%) than in a historical control group (6%)28, was also more frequently in both PCS patient cohorts with 17% and 23%28.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Symptoms of MCAS 'significantly mirror those of individuals with Long COVID' — a shared clinical-feature comparison, not an assertion that patients carry both diagnoses.

label: shared_mechanism

provenance_quote: In particular, extracellular vesicles are seen as a highly discriminating accompaniment to ME/CFS [434], and are being observed in both acute [435] and Long COVID-19 [436] patients.

label: shared_mechanism

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Reports 'a strong linear relationship between skin extensibility and POTS in patients with hEDS', linking an EDS physical marker to POTS rather than simply asserting prevalence of comorbidity.

provenance_quote: Wandele et al. reported a strong linear relationship between skin extensibility and POST in patients with hEDS. They also noted that, when compared with other factors, skin extensibility was the most predictive for POST [10].

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: States 'neurocognitive symptoms and OI overlap in ME/CFS', describing overlapping symptom domains within ME/CFS rather than asserting two separate comorbid diagnoses.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Reports a hallmark ME/CFS symptom (PEM) occurring in COVID patients, a symptom-overlap claim, not a diagnosis co-occurrence: 'one of the major ME/CFS symptoms, was observed in 56.8% of a sample of 3762 COVID-19 patients'.
finding_text: Post-exertional malaise, a hallmark ME/CFS symptom, was reported by 56.8% of a sample of 3762 COVID-19 patients surveyed across 56 countries.
provenance_quote: Post-exertional malaise, one of the major ME/CFS symptoms, was observed in 56.8% of a sample of 3762 COVID-19 patients across 56 countries [28].

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Links GJH to resting heart rate (an autonomic physiological marker), not a diagnosed dysautonomia comorbidity: 'heart rate at 14 years was significantly associated with...GJH at age 14 years'.
finding_text: After correcting for age and BMI, higher resting heart rate at age 14 was significantly associated with presence of GJH at age 14.
provenance_quote: After correcting for age and BMI, heart rate at 14 years was significantly associated with both GJH at age 14 years (OR: 1.01 (95% CI: 1.01 to 1.02); p<0.001), and also with depression at 18 years (OR: 1.01 (95% CI: 1.00 to 1.02), p=0.007).

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Notes symptom overlap between the conditions to justify using an ME/CFS-derived model: 'overlapping symptoms of Long COVID to ME/CFS', not a claim that patients carry both diagnoses.

provenance_quote: With overlapping symptoms of Long COVID to ME/CFS, this assessment may provide insights for additional efforts to understand the impact of Long COVID on students' education.

label: shared_mechanism

provenance_quote: Central sensitization, which was extreme in 69% of the patients (CSI score ≥60), was 1 of the main determinants of ESC abnormalities and was associated with a higher NPSI score, even though these 2 factors were not correlated.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Compares gut microbiome marker (Firmicutes/Bacteroidetes ratio) findings between IBS and FM literature as a mechanistic link, not a claim that patients have both: 'IBS is associated with a high...ratio...whereas in a study...FM...a low...ratio was observed'.

provenance_quote: IBS is associated with a high Firmicutes to Bacteroidetes ratio (45, 46) whereas in a study comparing 54 FM patients and 36 healthy individuals, a low Firmicutes to Bacteroidetes ratio (44) was observed.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: States sleep disorder prevalence separately within each condition ('33% in IBS...and 92.9% in FM') as a shared symptom-burden pattern, not a co-occurrence of the two diagnoses in the same patients.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Reports a statistical correlation of symptom scores between PASC and ME/CFS groups ('correlation of 0.729'), indicating overlapping symptom profiles rather than diagnosed co-occurrence.

provenance_quote: Symptom scores of the PASC group at time one and those for the ME/CFS group showed a correlation of 0.729 (p < 0.0001).

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Proposes a shared biological pathway (TGFB dysregulation) underlying circadian disruption in both conditions: 'circadian breakdown in ME/CFS and PASC as a consequence of changes in transforming growth factor beta'.
finding_text: Dysregulated TGFB (transforming growth factor beta) signaling, previously associated with ME/CFS especially in peripheral cells, is hypothesized to disrupt circadian physiological rhythms in sleep, activity, and cognition in ME/CFS and PASC.
provenance_quote: There is a possibility of a circadian breakdown in ME/CFS and PASC as a consequence of changes in transforming growth factor beta (TGFB), a cytokine previously associated with ME/CFS especially in peripheral cells [39].

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Reports long COVID patients' symptom rates (PEM, cognitive problems) as 'overlapping heavily with ME/CFS symptomatology', a symptom-overlap claim rather than dual-diagnosis comorbidity.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Describes autoantibody (anti-collagen/anti-TrM-03) network differences specific to the ME/CFS+FM subgroup, a biomarker-level link rather than a stated prevalence/co-occurrence claim.
finding_text: The ME/CFS(+)FM group showed an increase in the number of correlational associations of anti-collagen and anti-TrM-03 autoantibodies with other autoantibodies compared to controls.
provenance_quote: The ME/CFS(+)FM group was characterized by an increase in the number of associations of anti-collagen AAb and anti-TrM-03 AAb with other AAb.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Describes abolished anti-neural autoantibody correlations specific to ME/CFS(+)FM group, a biomarker network pattern rather than a comorbidity prevalence statement.
finding_text: In the ME/CFS(+)FM group, the normal intragroup correlations between anti-neural autoantibodies observed in healthy controls were abolished.
provenance_quote: Another feature of the AAb correlation pattern in the ME/CFS(+)FM group was the abolished intragroup correlations between anti-neural AAb.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Proposes autoantibodies to adrenergic/cholinergic receptors as a biological mechanism for autonomic dysfunction, linking long COVID/ME_CFS via shared biology rather than asserting patient co-occurrence.
finding_text: Prior literature suggests autonomic dysfunction in long COVID and ME/CFS is associated with autoantibodies against β-adrenergic and muscarinic cholinergic receptors.
provenance_quote: Cumulative evidence suggests that such autonomic dysfunction is associated with autoantibodies to β adrenergic and muscarinic cholinergic receptors [22, 23].

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Describes a symptom cluster (fatigue, PEM, brain fog, unrefreshing sleep) in PASC that resembles the ME/CFS phenotype, a shared symptom-pattern link rather than an explicit named-condition co-occurrence statement in this quote.
finding_text: Principal component analysis showed that fatigue, post-exertional malaise, daytime sleepiness, brain fog, and unrefreshing sleep clustered together as co-occurring symptoms resembling ME/CFS.
provenance_quote: The analysis suggests that fatigue, PEM, daytime sleepiness (lethargy), brain fog, and unrefreshing sleep were likely to occur together.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: 'demonstrated the biological overlap of ME/CFS and long COVID through TRPM3 ion channel dysfunction' explicitly frames the link as shared biology/mechanism, not patient co-occurrence.
finding_text: The discussion cites a prior study showing TRPM3 ion channel dysfunction as a biological overlap between ME/CFS and long COVID, noting TRPM3 is highly expressed in the brainstem, potentially explaining shared brainstem pathology.
provenance_quote: Further, a recent investigation demonstrated the biological overlap of ME/CFS and long COVID through transient receptor potential melastatin 3 (TRPM3) ion channel dysfunction (Sasso et al., 2022).

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: 'Naltrexone ... has some utility for addressing symptoms in both fibromyalgia and ME/CFS' links the two conditions via a shared treatment-responsive pathway, not a comorbidity/co-occurrence claim.
finding_text: The addition of low-dose naltrexone was associated with an improvement in energy and overall function in this patient.
provenance_quote: We added naltrexone, which has some utility for addressing symptoms in both fibromyalgia and ME/CFS [40,41,42]. This was associated with an improvement in energy and overall function

label: shared_mechanism

finding_text: ME/CFS shares common pathophysiological mechanisms with other neuroinflammatory conditions such as depression, fibromyalgia, and migraine, including HPA axis alterations, cytokine-mediated inflammatory signaling, dysregulated monoamines, and excessive glutamatergic transmission with compromised GABAergic inhibition.
provenance_quote: Myalgic encephalitis (ME)/CFS are two other maladies associated with mitochondrial dysfunction. The two pathologies show common mechanisms with neuroinflammatory diseases, such as depression, fibromyalgia, and migraine.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Reports increased mast cell number and IL-1β in cerebral cortex of a fibromyalgia animal model, a mechanistic mast-cell link to FM pathophysiology rather than a comorbid-patient claim.
finding_text: Cerebral cortex of fibromyalgia model rats showed an increase in mast cell number compared to controls, accompanied by increased IL-1β immuno-expression.
provenance_quote: an increase in mast cell number and IL-1β immune-expression.

label: shared_mechanism

finding_text: The paper notes significant symptom overlap between long COVID and myalgic encephalomyelitis, with fatigue as a major shared component, suggesting a shared pathophysiology potentially involving neuroimmune exhaustion.
provenance_quote: There is a significant overlap in symptoms of long COVID and ME, with fatigue being a major component in both.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Describes shared COL1A1/COL1A2 genetic variants producing an "osteogenesis imperfecta/EDS overlap" phenotype, a mechanistic/genetic overlap rather than an assertion that patients carry two independent diagnoses.
finding_text: Specific variants in COL1A1 and COL1A2 are associated with an osteogenesis imperfecta/EDS overlap phenotype, proposed as a possible fifteenth EDS type (COL1-related overlap disorder).
provenance_quote: Two years later, renewed attention focused on the so-called osteogenesis imperfecta/EDS overlap due to specific variants in COL1A1 and COL1A2. label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Proposes inflammation and glial dysfunction as "shared pathobiological hallmarks underlying both post-COVID-19 syndrome and ME/CFS", a mechanism-sharing claim.
finding_text: The authors propose that chronic systemic and central nervous system inflammation together with dysfunctional glial reactivity are shared pathobiological hallmarks underlying both post-COVID-19 syndrome and ME/CFS.
provenance_quote: Chronic inflammation and glial pathological reactivity are common hallmarks of several neurodegenerative and neuropsychiatric disorders and have been consistently associated with reduced central and peripheral levels of plasmalogens

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Proposes a single therapy (plasmalogen replacement) for both ME/CFS and post-COVID-19 syndrome based on a presumed common underlying deficit, implying shared mechanism rather than patient co-occurrence.
finding_text: The authors propose plasmalogen replacement therapy (PRT) as a potentially simple, effective, and safe strategy to relieve debilitating symptoms of ME/CFS and post-COVID-19 syndrome, based on promising outcomes of PRT in other neurodegenerative/neuropsychiatric disorders.
provenance_quote: Along with the promising outcomes of plasmalogen replacement therapy (PRT) for various neurodegenerative/neuropsychiatric disorders, we sought to propose PRT as a simple, effective, and safe strategy for the potential relief of the debilitating symptoms associated with ME/CFS and post-COVID-19 syndrome.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Shows the same heart-rate-to-reaction-time relationship holding independently "in both the PASC ... and < 4 years ME/CFS cohorts", a shared physiological mechanism across two separate cohorts, not comorbid patients.
finding_text: In participants aged 40 years or older, change in heart rate during the orthostatic challenge significantly mediated slowed procedural reaction time in both the PASC and <4-year ME/CFS cohorts.
provenance_quote: This model found that a change in HR during the NLT was associated with slowed PRT in both the PASC (Figure 4C) and < 4 years ME/CFS cohorts (Figure 4D) in the ≥40 years group (PASC: −1.7, non-parametric bootstrap 95% CI: (−4.0.4, −0.04), p = 0.04 and ME/CFS <4 years: −2.4, non-parametric bootstrap 95% CI: (−6.2, −0.1), p = 0.03).

label: shared_mechanism

provenance_quote: Emerging data suggest that CFS and fibromyalgia are associated with deficiencies of CoQ10 and NADH, both of which play a pivotal role in mitochondrial ATP production and cellular metabolism homeostasis [5].

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Claim centers on a shared heritable/genetic factor ('a common, heritable component to IC and other nociplastic ... conditions') rather than reporting patient-level co-occurrence rates.
finding_text: The overall pattern of results supports a shared, heritable component underlying interstitial cystitis and its comorbid nociplastic pain and psychiatric conditions (fibromyalgia, IBS, ME/CFS, major depressive disorder, panic disorder).
provenance_quote: Our results support a common, heritable component to IC and other nociplastic and psychiatric conditions.

label: shared_mechanism

finding_text: A proposed mechanism links chronic joint hypermobility in EDS to migraine via stimulation of cervical afferents and activation of the trigeminal cervical complex.
provenance_quote: one reported pathway appears to be associated with chronic joint hypermobility, which stimulates cervical afferents resulting in the activation of the trigeminal cervical complex and subsequent development of head pain

label: shared_mechanism

label: shared_mechanism

provenance_quote: Although numerous studies have suggested antibiotic usage is not associated with disease development in both PACS and ME/CFS, more studies are warranted to investigate the role of antibiotics in the PAISs, and antibiotic usage should be taken as a potential covariable in the analysis.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: States clinical symptom overlap ('fatigue, post-exertional malaise, and cognitive impairment') between ME/CFS and PCC motivating cross-application of clinical knowledge — a shared-presentation/mechanism argument, not a comorbidity statistic.

provenance_quote: In patients with IBS, increased abundance of unclassified Alistipes and decreased Faecalibacterium were reported, while in patients without IBS, increased unclassified Bacteroides abundance and decreased Bacteroides vulgatus were biomarkers of ME/CFS.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Text links the two illnesses via a shared biological correlate: 'brain neurochemical levels were associated with self-reported severity measures in long COVID and ME/CFS', not a claim of patients having both.
finding_text: Brain neurochemical levels measured by MRS were associated with self-reported severity measures in both long COVID and ME/CFS patients.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Text describes symptom overlap and a shared hypothesized mechanism ('dysregulated immune response and hyperinflammation') between long COVID and ME/CFS, not a patient-level co-occurrence claim.
finding_text: The paper discusses that a large symptom overlap exists between long COVID and ME/CFS core criteria (fatigue, reduced daily activity, post-exertional malaise), with both syndromes hypothesized to originate from a dysregulated immune response and hyperinflammation.
provenance_quote: A review and comparison of symptomatology between long COVID and Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS) sheds light on the large overlap of symptoms reported by long COVID studies and the major criteria symptoms for ME/CFS (fatigue, reduced daily activity, and post-exertional malaise).

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Text describes hEDS patients being 'frequently misdiagnosed as having fibromyalgia' due to overlapping symptoms, a symptom-overlap/misdiagnosis mechanism rather than an assertion that patients have both diagnoses.

provenance_quote: In a survey conducted by Donohue et al. (2018), for example, it was observed that hEDS patients are frequently misdiagnosed as having fibromyalgia.

label: shared_mechanism

finding_text: ME/CFS and post-COVID ME/CFS patients had worse sleep quality than matched healthy controls.
provenance_quote: Patients showed lower activity and worse sleep quality than matched healthy controls, together with a worse lipid profile than controls, that was associated with disturbances in the circadian temperature rhythm.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: ICAM-1/lipid association differs in patients (combined ME/CFS and post-COVID group) vs controls, a biomarker/mechanism finding not a patient comorbidity claim.
finding_text: ICAM-1 levels were associated with plasma lipids in healthy controls but not in ME/CFS/post-COVID patients.
provenance_quote: ICAM-1 levels were associated with plasma lipids in healthy controls, but not in patients, who showed higher levels of endothelin-1 and VCAM-1.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Elevated endothelin-1 is reported as a shared biomarker of endothelial dysfunction across ME/CFS and post-COVID ME/CFS patients, not a claim of two co-occurring diagnoses.
finding_text: ME/CFS and post-COVID ME/CFS patients showed higher levels of endothelin-1 than healthy controls, suggestive of endothelial dysfunction.
provenance_quote: ICAM-1 levels were associated with plasma lipids in healthy controls, but not in patients, who showed higher levels of endothelin-1 and VCAM-1.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Elevated VCAM-1 is reported as a shared endothelial-dysfunction marker across ME/CFS and post-COVID ME/CFS patients, a mechanistic link rather than comorbidity assertion.
finding_text: ME/CFS and post-COVID ME/CFS patients showed higher levels of VCAM-1 than healthy controls, suggestive of endothelial dysfunction.
provenance_quote: ICAM-1 levels were associated with plasma lipids in healthy controls, but not in patients, who showed higher levels of endothelin-1 and VCAM-1.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Orthostatic intolerance (a dysautonomia symptom) is reported as one of the frequently-reported ME/CFS symptom-criteria items, reflecting symptom overlap rather than an explicit two-condition comorbidity claim.
finding_text: Across both COVID-19 groups, unrefreshing sleep was the most frequently reported individual ME/CFS symptom, followed by postexertional malaise and orthostatic intolerance.
provenance_quote: In both the COVID-19–positive group and the COVID-19–negative group, unrefreshing sleep was the most frequently reported ME/CFS symptom (range, 20.2%-26.3%), followed by postexertional malaise (range, 16.9%-22.4%) and orthostatic intolerance (range, 9.0%-13.1%).

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Proposes a shared 'connectionist... biological basis' explaining symptom overlap across syndromes, not that patients carry both diagnoses.
finding_text: The pattern of variable, largely non-overlapping symptom clusters across long-COVID, CFS, IBS, fibromyalgia and severe asthma is inconsistent with a modular causal structure but is consistent with a connectionist (parallel distributed processing) biological basis for medically unexplained symptoms, which could explain symptom overlap between syndromes, absence of a diagnostic biomarker, and efficacy of psychological/behavioral interventions.
provenance_quote: Although the symptom networks of long-COVID and CFS differ, the variation of cluster content across the six groups is inconsistent with a modular causal structure but consistent with a connectionist (network, parallel distributed processing) biological basis of MUS.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Identifies 'bridge symptoms' connecting internalizing and functional-disorder (ME/CFS/FM/IBS) symptom networks, a mechanistic/network link rather than a comorbidity claim.
finding_text: Fatigue, difficulty concentrating, trouble sleeping, and unrefreshing sleep were the most centrally connected 'bridge symptoms' linking internalizing disorder (MDD/GAD) and functional disorder (ME/CFS/FM/IBS) symptom domains.
provenance_quote: Fatigue, concentration problems, and trouble sleeping presented with the greatest number of connections, ranging from 29 to 33 (Fig. 2). In general, the overlapping symptoms had the most connections: fatigue with 86.8%, concentration problems with 76.3%, trouble sleeping with 76.3%, and unrefreshing sleep with 71.1% of all other symptoms.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: A COL1A1 variant of unknown significance is proposed to link hEDS to an 'osteogenesis imperfecta/EDS overlap disorder', a genetic-mechanism hypothesis in a single patient, not an established comorbidity.
finding_text: A variant of unknown significance in COL1A1 was identified in a patient fulfilling hEDS criteria, potentially associated with an osteogenesis imperfecta/EDS overlap disorder or arthrochalasia EDS.
provenance_quote: However, in a patient, fulfilling the 2017 hEDS criteria, a variant of unknown significance was identified in COL1A1 (c.Gly697Thr), which may be associated with osteogenesis imperfecta/EDS overlap disorder or arthrochalasia EDS.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Links long COVID and Gulf War Illness to ME/CFS via a shared biomarker (NK cell dysfunction) and 'similar symptom profiles', not a comorbidity claim.
finding_text: NK cell dysfunction has also been reported in long COVID and Gulf War Illness, conditions with symptom profiles overlapping ME/CFS, suggesting shared immune mechanisms warranting further investigation.
provenance_quote: NK cell dysfunction has been reported in long COVID (151) and Gulf War Illness (122, 152) that have similar symptom profiles.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: States the two conditions 'exhibit overlapping symptoms' causing diagnostic difficulty, a phenotypic/mechanistic overlap rather than an assertion that patients have both.
finding_text: Post-COVID-19 condition and ME/CFS have overlapping symptoms, which creates diagnostic challenges in distinguishing between the two conditions.
provenance_quote: Post-COVID-19 condition and ME/CFS can exhibit overlapping symptoms, thus leading to challenges in distinguishing between them; moreover, both conditions are associated with substantial decreases in quality of life and occupational participation.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: A quantitative sensory test (cold detection threshold, a small-fiber function marker) correlates with pain/disability severity in FMS, a mechanistic link rather than a stated co-diagnosis.
finding_text: Cold detection threshold was negatively correlated with weekly pain severity and functional impairment (rFIQ function domain) in both male and female patients, suggesting small fibre pathology contributes to pain and disability.
provenance_quote: Loss of function in CDT was associated with higher scores in AWP and severe functional impairment in both men and women.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Links MCAS and hEDS via a proposed biological mechanism: 'histamine-activated mitochondrial ROS production has been shown to exacerbate mitochondrial dysfunction... relevant in patients with MCAS often associated with hEDS' - a mechanism-centered claim rather than a direct patient comorbidity assertion.
finding_text: Histamine-activated mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS) production has been shown to exacerbate mitochondrial dysfunction, which may be particularly relevant in MCAS patients often associated with hEDS.
provenance_quote: Furthermore, histamine-activated mitochondrial ROS production has been shown to exacerbate mitochondrial dysfunction [29,45], which may be particularly relevant in patients with MCAS often associated with hEDS [29].

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Mitochondrial ROS/dysfunction mechanism 'relevant in patients with MCAS often associated with hEDS' - mechanism-centered link (duplicate of C0524).
finding_text: Histamine-activated mitochondrial reactive oxygen species production has been shown to exacerbate mitochondrial dysfunction, which may be particularly relevant in patients with MCAS often associated with hEDS.
provenance_quote: Furthermore, histamine-activated mitochondrial ROS production has been shown to exacerbate mitochondrial dysfunction [29,45], which may be particularly relevant in patients with MCAS often associated with hEDS [29].

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Hypothesizes mitochondrial ATP/dysfunction underlying 'heightened mast cell reactivity' and FcεRI activation; hEDS is only inferred from case context, not explicitly named in this specific sentence, so confidence is low.
finding_text: Hypothetical mitochondrial dysfunction may explain heightened mast cell reactivity in the patient, as adequate ATP levels are essential for mast cell function and FcεRI-dependent activation, and MT-ATP6 variants are associated with increased susceptibility to infections and immune-mediated complications.
provenance_quote: The hypothetical mitochondrial dysfunction may explain the heightened mast cell reactivity observed in our patient, as adequate ATP levels are essential for proper mast cell function and FcεRI-dependent activation [53].

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Describes hypermobility as a physical trait linked to movement inefficiency within a JFS cohort ('hypermobility was associated with greater movement inefficiencies'), not a comorbidity diagnosis claim; effect was non-significant overall.
finding_text: Despite lacking overall statistical significance versus non-hypermobile JFS peers, hypermobility was associated with greater movement inefficiencies during landing/jumping, suggesting a need for hypermobility-specific movement assessment.
provenance_quote: This study highlights the need for hypermobility-specific movement assessments to understand movement-associated pain, strength, and kinesthetics to improve early identification and treatment of youth with hypermobility at risk for chronic pain and functional limitations.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Cites prior work that 'a higher need for control is associated with both CFS and FM', a shared psychological trait/mechanism rather than a claim that patients have both diagnoses.
finding_text: Prior published research cited by the authors reported that a higher need for control is associated with both chronic fatigue syndrome and fibromyalgia.
provenance_quote: a higher need for control is associated with both CFS and FM (Keen et al., 2022).

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Authors 'propose systemic dysautonomia and psychosomatic factors as contributors' to the abdominal-pain/migraine association — a proposed shared mechanism, not a claim that patients carry a dysautonomia diagnosis alongside migraine.
finding_text: Chronic abdominal pain was significantly associated with the presence of migraines in this cohort, suggesting a shared systemic dysautonomic or psychosomatic mechanism.
provenance_quote: Notably, chronic abdominal pain was significantly associated with the presence of migraines (p = 0.045). After excluding organic causes, we propose systemic dysautonomia and psychosomatic factors as contributors, a novel insight emphasizing the complexity of this population.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Authors hypothesize 'neuroimmune or inflammatory pathways contribute to the broader hEDS/HSD phenotype', framing autonomic dysfunction as part of a shared mechanistic overlap rather than asserting a quantified patient comorbidity.
finding_text: The authors hypothesize that the observed high prevalence of immune dysregulation, autonomic dysfunction, and gastrointestinal dysmotility supports the possibility that neuroimmune or inflammatory pathways contribute to the broader hEDS/HSD phenotype, suggesting overlap with autoimmune or autoinflammatory conditions rather than purely connective tissue pathology.
provenance_quote: Although speculative and beyond the causal scope of this cross-sectional survey, these findings suggest that hEDS may, in some cases, reflect overlapping features with autoimmune or autoinflammatory conditions rather than representing a purely connective tissue–based pathophysiology.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Overlap between fibromyalgia and IBS is attributed to 'central sensitization, reinforcing the functional symptom pattern' — a mechanistic claim, not a quantified comorbidity.
finding_text: Overlapping somatic complaints such as fibromyalgia and IBS in PNES patients were proposed by reviewed literature to reflect central sensitization mechanisms that reinforce the functional symptom pattern.
provenance_quote: These overlapping complaints contribute to central sensitization, reinforcing the functional symptom pattern [105].

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Fibromyalgia and IBS-type disturbance are linked via 'interoceptive distortion and heightened autonomic responsivity' as proposed common mechanistic threads, not a patient co-occurrence claim.
finding_text: A review by Carle-Toulemonde et al. proposed that interoceptive distortion and heightened autonomic responsivity serve as common mechanistic threads linking functional somatic syndromes (e.g., fibromyalgia, IBS-type GI disturbance) with functional neurological disorders.
provenance_quote: Carle-Toulemonde et al. [40] provided a compelling review linking functional somatic syndromes with functional neurological disorders, describing how interoceptive distortion and heightened autonomic responsivity may serve as common threads.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: HPA-axis cortisol dysregulation is described as a mechanism 'particularly evident in ME/CFS' that 'can lead to ... autonomic dysfunction' as one of several downstream symptoms — a mechanistic explanation, not a comorbidity prevalence claim.
finding_text: Low cortisol levels and altered cortisol rhythms (hypocortisolism) are particularly evident in ME/CFS, associated with a dysregulated stress response that can lead to fatigue, PEM, autonomic dysfunction, and sleep disturbances.
provenance_quote: Hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal axis neuroendocrine dysregulation, characterized by low cortisol levels (hypocortisolism) and altered cortisol rhythms is particularly evident in individuals with ME/CFS, where a dysregulated stress response can lead to unexplainable fatigue, post-exertional malaise, autonomic dysfunction, and sleep disturbances, among other core symptoms [107].

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: A cited study on venous-origin pelvic pain (56% with EDS/HSD) showed symptom improvement after vascular-compression surgery, 'across symptoms overlapping with ME/CFS and long COVID' — a speculative shared (vascular) mechanism, not a direct diagnosed-comorbidity claim.
finding_text: A cited study of women with venous-origin chronic pelvic pain (56% with EDS or hypermobility spectrum disorder) found substantial symptomatic improvement after surgical treatment of vascular compression, across symptoms overlapping with ME/CFS and long COVID.
provenance_quote: A study of 45 women with venous origin chronic pelvic pain found substantial improvement from surgical treatment in a broad range of symptoms overlapping with ME/CFS and long COVID; 56% of these patients had EDS or hypermobility spectrum disorder.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: A fibromyalgia-risk genetic variant lies near MDGA2, a gene whose 'haploinsufficiency is associated with autism spectrum disorder' — a shared genetic locus, not a patient co-occurrence claim.
finding_text: Variants in MAML3 (Notch pathway coactivator) and near MDGA2 (synaptic organization gene linked to autism spectrum disorder haploinsufficiency) were associated with fibromyalgia risk.
provenance_quote: MDGA2 haploinsufficiency is associated with autism spectrum disorder88,89.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: A fibromyalgia-risk variant near BCL11A, whose 'haploinsufficiency causes intellectual disability and autism' — a shared genetic locus linking the conditions mechanistically.
finding_text: A variant near BCL11A, a transcription factor whose haploinsufficiency causes intellectual disability and autism, was associated with fibromyalgia risk.
provenance_quote: Besides its canonical role in hematopoiesis and repression of fetal hemoglobin in adults, BCL11A has neurodevelopmental roles, and haploinsufficiency causes intellectual disability and autism98–100.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: 'genetic overlap extended to ... hypermobility syndrome (rg = 0.79, p = 8.4 × 10−13)' — a genetic correlation (shared biology) statistic, not a stated patient comorbidity.
finding_text: Fibromyalgia showed a strong genetic correlation with hypermobility syndrome, as well as with trochanteric bursitis.
provenance_quote: Furthermore, this genetic overlap extended to related musculoskeletal conditions like trochanteric bursitis (rg = 0.82, p = 3.1 × 10−21) and hypermobility syndrome (rg = 0.79, p = 8.4 × 10−13).

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Same genetic correlation finding: fibromyalgia showed 'strong genetic correlation with hypermobility syndrome' (rg = 0.79) — shared genetic architecture, not an asserted patient co-occurrence.
finding_text: Fibromyalgia showed strong genetic correlation with hypermobility syndrome and trochanteric bursitis.
provenance_quote: Furthermore, this genetic overlap extended to related musculoskeletal conditions like trochanteric bursitis (rg = 0.82, p = 3.1 × 10−21) and hypermobility syndrome (rg = 0.79, p = 8.4 × 10−13).

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Risk loci overlap across conditions suggests "shared genetic factors or diagnostic overlap" between fibromyalgia, long COVID and ME/CFS, not patient-level co-diagnosis.
finding_text: Certain fibromyalgia risk loci overlapped (with different lead variants) with previously reported long COVID risk loci (BPTF) and ME/CFS risk loci (OLFM4, RABGAP1L/GPR52), suggesting possible shared genetic factors or diagnostic overlap between these poorly characterized conditions.
provenance_quote: Additionally, certain risk loci overlapped with long COVID120 (BPTF) and ME/CFS121 (OLFM4, RABGAP1L/GPR52), two poorly characterized disorders, albeit with different lead variants.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: A single participant's pathogenic MYH7 myopathy variant is described as "consistent with a myopathy causing exercise intolerance, fatigue, dyspnea, dysautonomia" — a mechanistic case description, not a population comorbidity claim.
finding_text: A pathogenic MYH7 variant affecting cardiac myosin heavy chain was found in one participant, consistent with a myopathy causing exercise intolerance, fatigue, dyspnea, dysautonomia and neck pain.
provenance_quote: Participant 25 carried a pathogenic MYH7 variant affecting the cardiac myosin heavy chain [117].

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Links trauma to "central sensitization symptoms across the nociplastic pain spectrum (migraine, fibromyalgia...)", a shared-mechanism claim, not a patient co-occurrence claim.
finding_text: Traumatic experiences were significantly associated with central sensitization symptoms across the nociplastic pain spectrum (migraine, fibromyalgia, comorbid FM-CM), independent of diagnostic group.
provenance_quote: TEs were significantly associated to CS symptoms across the NP spectrum (a: b = .31; p < .05), independently of condition.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Describes SNPs/genes associated with ME/CFS that were "replicated in post-viral fatigue and fibromyalgia" — a shared genetic mechanism, not a patient comorbidity claim.
finding_text: A UK Biobank ME/CFS analysis found 199 SNPs mapped to 14 genes across 15 clusters significantly associated with 91% of ME/CFS cases, implicating stress/infection susceptibility, mitochondrial dysfunction, sleep disorders, and autoimmune development, replicated in post-viral fatigue and fibromyalgia cohorts.
provenance_quote: Another study, through a combined analysis of ME/CFS cohorts in the UK Biobank, found 199 SNPs mapped to 14 genes that were significantly associated with 91% of ME/CFS cases, and these SNPs were grouped into 15 clusters involving multiple genes associated with key cellular mechanisms of CFS.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Mouse-model finding that imatinib "abolished F. nucleatum-induced mast cell activation and prevented elevation of visceral sensitivity" links mast cell activation mechanistically to gut hypersensitivity, not patient comorbidity.
finding_text: Imatinib, a tyrosine kinase inhibitor targeting Cd117 that depletes mast cells, abolished F. nucleatum-induced mast cell activation and prevented elevation of visceral sensitivity.
provenance_quote: imatinib treatment abolished the stimulatory effect of F. nucleatum on mast cell activation (Figure S3C–F), and significantly prevented the elevation of visceral sensitivity in ABX mice monoassociated with F. nucleatum (Figure S3G–I).

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Mast cell stabilizer sodium cromoglicate reduced mast cell activation and visceral sensitivity in an animal model, a mechanistic link, not a patient co-occurrence claim.
finding_text: The mast cell stabilizer sodium cromoglicate largely abolished F. nucleatum-induced mast cell activation and prevented elevation of visceral sensitivity and defecation frequency.
provenance_quote: Sodium cromoglicate largely abolished the stimulatory effect of F. nucleatum on mast cell activation (Figures 3E–G, S4A). Sodium cromoglicate treatment also significantly prevented the elevation of visceral sensitivity and defecation frequency in ABX mice monoassociated with F. nucleatum (Figures 3H, S4B).

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Allopurinol reduced uric acid, mast cell activation markers, and visceral sensitivity in mice, a mechanistic pathway link rather than a comorbidity assertion.
finding_text: Allopurinol, a xanthine oxidase inhibitor, reduced uric acid levels, mast cell activation markers, and visceral sensitivity in F. nucleatum-monoassociated ABX mice.
provenance_quote: we pharmacologically inhibited uric acid production using allopurinol in F. nucleatum-treated ABX mice (Figure 4D–E), a xanthine oxidase inhibitor, observing a simultaneous reduction in mast cell activation (Figure 4F–I). Moreover, allopurinol treatment also significantly prevented the elevation of visceral sensitivity in ABX mice monoassociated with F. nucleatum (Figure 4J).

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: Describes fibromyalgia as 'a condition that shares substantial clinical features with ME/CFS' in the context of treatment mechanism (taVNS/HRV biofeedback), a shared-features/mechanism statement rather than a patient co-occurrence claim.
finding_text: In early pilot studies of fibromyalgia, transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) and HRV biofeedback were associated with improvements in autonomic function, pain symptoms, and subjective cognitive clarity.
provenance_quote: In early pilot studies involving patients with fibromyalgia, a condition that shares substantial clinical features with ME/CFS, both taVNS and HRV biofeedback have been associated with improvements in autonomic function, pain symptoms, and subjective cognitive clarity.

label: shared_mechanism
rationale: States TCAs/SNRIs show efficacy 'particularly in neuropathic pain, fibromyalgia, and irritable bowel syndrome', linking the conditions via a shared pharmacological/mechanistic response rather than asserting patient co-occurrence.
finding_text: Tricyclic antidepressants and SNRIs show greater analgesic efficacy than SSRIs, particularly for neuropathic pain, fibromyalgia, and irritable bowel syndrome.
provenance_quote: Clinically, tricyclic antidepressants and SNRIs (serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors) demonstrate superior analgesic efficacy compared with SSRIs, particularly in neuropathic pain, fibromyalgia, and irritable bowel syndrome.
